thread:
maria: seeing apiserver leader flapping across control-plane nodes in us-west-2, started ~10m ago. spike in apiserver 5xxs and controller-manager restarts :grimacing:

tj: pulling up grafana... etdc leader switches every ~90-120s, election latency spikes around the same time. attaching quick logs in a sec.

sam: also noticed NAT gateway CPU at 95% and a bunch of failed image pulls from our public registry around the same window. could be egress saturation.

alex: kube-controller-manager logs show repeated Get/Watch timeouts against apiserver and leader-election renew failures. stack looks like: controller-manager -> apiserver -> etcd.

maria: hmm this started around the same time the Dedicated autoscaler ran a bulk GPU provisioning job (batch of 40 nodes) for overnight training. those nodes pull 3GB model blobs each.

sam: yep, image pull/cached model downloads would hit NAT + s3 egress. we currently have single NAT GW per AZ. bursts will exhaust TCP ephemeral ports on the NAT appliance/router and increase RTTs.

eng-sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0412 - apiserver leader flapping in us-west-2. Severity: P2. Owner: eng-sre-oncall.

tj: quick mitigation idea: throttle model downloads (limit concurrency on the autoscaler job) and switch heavy pulls to our VPC endpoint/private registry mirror. can we patch the autoscaler config?

alex: we can add `maxParallelProvisioning: 8` to the GPU autoscaler pool for now. Also enabling `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` where possible.

maria: good. can someone run `kubectl get endpoints -n kube-system` and `ss -tan | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l` on the control-plane NAT host? want to validate port exhaustion.

sam: running commands now:
```
# on nat-host-1
ss -s
State      Recv-Q Send-Q
ESTAB      1023   0
TIME-WAIT  12456  0

# kube endpoints
kubectl get endpoints kube-apiserver -n kube-system -o yaml | yq .
```
TIME-WAIT count is high (~12k). looks like ephemeral port churn.

tj: that matches. kernel ephemeral port range + NAT source ports exhausted -> new connections get RSTs -> longer apiserver latencies -> leader election timeouts.

maria: mitigation tasks: 1) reduce provisioning parallelism, 2) enable registry mirror + S3 VPC endpoint, 3) add second NAT gateway or switch to NAT GW autoscaling, 4) short-term firewall rules to deprioritize large outbound pulls. agree?

alex: agree. I'll open a quick PR to autoscaler with `maxParallelProvisioning` and patch the job def to use the mirror host.

sam: I'll create NAT autoscale request with infra + add a route to the S3 VPC endpoint. also recommend enabling tcp_tw_reuse and bumping `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` on nat hosts as a stopgap.

maria: note on tradeoffs: adding NATs costs ~$600/mo per AZ; registry mirror + S3 VPC endpoint is cheaper but requires infra work and warm cache. need cost estimate for both.

tj: preliminary cost callout: extra NAT GW per AZ =~ $400-800/mo depending on hours and data. S3 VPC endpoint data charges same but no per-hour appliance. Mirror (ECR) cache + replication ~ add storage + transfer but usually cheaper at scale.

deploy-bot: deploy started: autoscaler-config PR #482 -> staging (maria). Status: success.

alex: autoscaler patch deployed to staging. lowering concurrency from 40 -> 8. monitoring for apiserver 503s.

maria: after patch: apiserver 5xxs dropped by ~70% in the last 6m, controller-manager stopped restarting. etcd leader switches reduced to 1 per 10m.

sam: NAT host TW counts dropping, kernel tweaks applied on nat-host-1: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"10240 65535\"`. port exhaustion eased.

tj: long-term: implement image mirror + pre-warming for model blobs, autoscaler backoff logic, and consider per-customer egress quotas to prevent noisy provisioning from impacting control plane.

maria: creating follow-up infra tickets:
- INFRA-2241 Add ECR mirror + pre-warm pipeline (owner: sam)
- INFRA-2242 NAT autoscale / second NAT GW in us-west-2 (owner: infra)
- SRE-319 apiserver leader flapping post-mortem + playbook updates (owner: tj)

alex: note to product: please advise ML teams to use the mirror for scheduled bulk provisioning or spread provisioning across windows. cc @ml-platform.

maria: any objections to closing incident and moving to post-mortem? current SLO impact reduced.

tj: fine to close incident, track in post-mortem. :thumbsup:

eng-sre-bot: incident INC-2026-0412 status updated -> Resolved. Follow-ups logged.

sam: quick aside: we should also add metrics for NAT ephemeral port usage and `apiserver->etcd` latency correlation to alert earlier. I'll add a dashboard tile.

maria: agreed. thanks everyone. follow-ups in ticket INFRA-2241/2242/SRE-319. :white_check_mark:
